name: Vijayaraghava Perumal Temple, Thiruputkuzhi
deity: Vishnu as Vijayaraghava Perumal, with the Goddess Maragathavalli Thayar
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Pandya, by local account (with later additions)
summary: At Thiruputkuzhi, west of Kanchipuram, Vishnu is worshipped as Vijayaraghava Perumal, where Rama is remembered as performing the last rites of the great bird Jatayu — a Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu.

sections.history: Thiruputkuzhi is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Thondai Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar praised the Lord of this village. The village lies in Kanchipuram district, to the west of Kanchipuram town. Local account holds that the present temple was built by the Pandya kings in the thirteenth century, though the sanctity of the place is far older in memory. The village is also remembered as the birthplace of Yadava Prakasa, the teacher under whom the young Ramanuja first studied. It is a temple in its own right, set in a village rather than within the town.
sections.architecture: The presiding Lord here is Vijayaraghava Perumal, Rama as the victorious one, and the Goddess is worshipped as Maragathavalli Thayar. The sacred water of the village is the Jatayu Tirtham, named for the bird whose story gives the place its name. It is a village temple, simple in setting, whose interest lies less in grandeur than in the story it keeps.
sections.legends: The name Thiruputkuzhi holds the legend in its syllables: pul, the bird, and kuzhi, the pit. In the Ramayana, Jatayu, the great bird, fought Ravana to save Sita and fell wounded. Rama, searching for Sita, found him dying and performed his last rites. The sthala purana places that act of mercy here, and the Jatayu Tirtham is held sacred in this memory. Tradition tells that Rama is worshipped here as Vijayaraghava, the victorious one.
sections.festivals: Vaikunta Ekadashi is the great day of the Vaishnava year at this Divya Desam, and the verses of the Divya Prabandham are recited on festival days. Devotees of Rama may also seek out the days sacred to him. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: A visit here is a pilgrimage into the Ramayana. Stand by the Jatayu Tirtham and recall the story of the bird who gave his life for Sita; then enter the shrine of the Lord who performed his last rites. The village is quiet, a short drive west of Kanchipuram, and it pairs naturally with a day among the Divya Desams of the town.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi and festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruputkuzhi is a village in Kanchipuram district, roughly 10 km west of Kanchipuram town. Kanchipuram is the nearest large town and railhead; Chennai is the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and local buses connect the village with Kanchipuram; confirm the route locally.
